title: Environment Access Playbook: IAM Policies, RBAC Scoping, Audit Schema, and SIEM Mappings (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook codifies environment-specific IAM role scoping, RBAC v2 mapping, audit log schema expectations, SIEM export formats, and an evidence-automation runbook for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It is intended for security engineers, platform engineers, SREs, and solutions engineers executing customer onboarding or audits.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Access control and telemetry artifacts used to demonstrate least-privilege, auditability, and automated evidence collection for compliance reviews (SOC2 / ISO27001 readiness).
- Audience: eng-security, eng-platform, eng-private-deployments, customer-success (for dedicated/private onboarding), and compliance reviewers.

High-level guidance (one-line rules):
- Prefer environment-scoped roles (hosted/dedicated/private) over broad global roles.
- Split administration into config-management vs runtime-ops roles.
- All privileged actions must emit structured audit events with correlation_id, actor, resource, action, result, and request_context.
- SIEM exports should contain normalized fields and a mapping table is required per environment and per export sink (Elastic / Splunk / S3).
- Evidence automation must support time-bound snapshots (policy, ACLs, role bindings) and signed digests for tamper-evidence.

Canonical Roles (RBAC v2 constructs) and responsibilities:
- PlatformAdmin: full access to control plane metadata, billing metadata, and cross-environment routing. Not allowed to access customer content except via explicit support hooks.
- ClusterOperator: manage underlying compute and networking for Dedicated/Private. Can reboot nodes, rotate certs, and adjust autoscaling. No direct customer data access.
- ModelDeployEngineer: create/rollout model versions, configure quantization/build artifacts, control inference runtime flags for performance testing.
- RuntimeSRE: emergency escalation, throttles, circuit-breaker config, rollback trigger. Allowed to read runtime traces and anonymized payloads only for debugging (see masking rules).
- CustomerAdmin: per-customer tenant admin (only for dedicated/private). Can manage customer-specific keys, routes, and SLA configs. Cannot access other customers.
- ReadOnlyAuditor: read-only access to configs, role bindings, and audit logs. No ability to change policies.
- SupportAgent: scoped support window access via just-in-time elevation (JIT) with approval and automatic session recording.

Environment-specific scoping patterns:
1) Hosted (multi-tenant):
   - Default: most infra roles are split into region-scoped roles (e.g., PlatformAdmin-eu, PlatformAdmin-us).
   - Customer separation: customer metadata and keys are tenant-scoped; CustomerAdmin exists only in dedicated/private contexts and for hosted customers only a tenant-owner identity (no interactive console-level access).
   - Elevated actions (e.g., decrypt customer data) require two-person approval and an audit token with TTL.
   - Audit retention: 365 days hot, 3 years cold archive for compliance-required customers.

2) Dedicated (single-tenant but hosted by Redwood):
   - Role bindings are per-deployment (dedicated-<customer-id>-operator).
   - ClusterOperator and ModelDeployEngineer need access to the deployment control plane but are denied direct access to KMS-wrapped customer keys unless explicit support escalation is recorded.
   - SIEM exports: dedicated deployments must push a subset of audit events to the customer-managed SIEM endpoint and to Redwood central SIEM for platform telemetry. Mapping table required.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - Default: customer-owned control plane; Redwood roles limited to support-agreed identities.
   - Access model: assume-role via federated identity (SAML/OIDC) with short-lived tokens; minimal default privileges.
   - Evidence collection: remote evidence collection agents (signed snapshots) or offline evidence bundles depending on air-gap.

Least-privilege policy templates (snippets and examples) - examples are illustrative templates to be adapted per deployment:
- Minimal PlatformAdmin (hosted, region-scoped) - YAML/JSON-like policy sample:
  {
    "version": "1",
    "statements": [
      {"effect":"allow","action":["controlplane:Read","controlplane:List"],"resource":["arn:redwood:region:*:config/*"]},
      {"effect":"allow","action":["billing:View"],"resource":["arn:redwood::billing/*"]},
      {"effect":"deny","action":["data:Read","data:Decrypt"],"resource":["arn:redwood:tenant:*:data/*"]}
    ]
  }

- JIT SupportAgent elevation flow (template):
  - Requestor opens ticket in Zendesk/Jira -> includes customer id, justification, duration.
  - Ticket triggers OPA policy evaluation; if allowed, issue short-lived role badge (5-30 minutes) bound to session recording.
  - All JIT sessions must be recorded and a signed event emitted at session start/end to the audit stream.

Audit log schema (canonical fields) - required across all environments (each event must include these top-level fields in ISO8601/UTC where applicable):
- event_id (uuid-v4)
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- service (string, e.g., serving-runtime, control-plane, kms)
- environment (hosted|dedicated|private)
- region (string)
- actor_id (principal id, prefixed by type e.g., user:, svc:)
- actor_roles (list of role names)
- action (string, e.g., policy.bind, model.deploy, key.rotate, session.start)
- resource_type (string)
- resource_id (string)
- result (success|failure|partial)
- request_id (trace-id/correlation-id)
- request_context (freeform JSON encoded string: ip, user_agent, forwarded_for)
- change_set (short summary or diffs base64 compressed for large payloads)
- evidence_ref (s3:// or signed artifact id)

Masking and PII handling rules:
- Cleartext customer input payloads must never be logged in audit streams. Where runtime payloads are required for debugging, they must be redacted/masked and stored in a protected evidence bucket with KMS envelopes and strict ACLs.
- Use hash-prefixing for identifiers to allow debugging without exposing raw identifiers (e.g., hash(tenant_id) first8).

SIEM export formats and mapping guidance:
- Recommended canonical export is newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with the canonical fields above.
- Elastic mapping suggestions: event_id->keyword, timestamp->date, service->keyword, environment->keyword, action->keyword, actor_id->keyword, resource_type->keyword, result->keyword, request_id->keyword, request_context->object (flattened).
- Splunk: use _json export; ensure event_id and request_id are promoted to top-level fields for correlation.
- Syslog/CDM export: when required, include a JSON payload in the msg field and populate standard syslog pri/timestamp.

SIEM per-environment differences to enforce in ops playbooks:
- Hosted: redact customer payloads before central SIEM; push metadata and alerting-worthy events (failures, escalations, JIT sessions).
- Dedicated: push all control-plane audits and selected runtime ops events to both customer and central SIEM. Provide customer with mapping doc for their SIEM onboarding.
- Private: support either push (customer-managed collector) or pull (signed evidence bundles) depending on network posture. Document allowed ports/URIs and signing keys out-of-band.

Evidence automation runbook (snapshot + signing + ingestion):
1) Trigger types: periodic (daily/weekly), on-demand (audit request), and event-driven (post-incident or after JIT session).
2) Snapshots captured: role-bindings, active tokens, policy versions, KMS rotation logs, route tables, SIEM export config, supported config digests.
3) Packaging: create a gzip bundle, compute SHA256, sign with Redwood evidence key (or customer key for private), and upload to hardened object store with immutable retention policy.
4) Metadata record: emit an audit event with evidence_ref and signed digest. Evidence must include human-readable manifest and machine-parseable index (CSV).
5) Retention: default 1 year for routine snapshots, extendable to 7 years for compliance-specific customers.

Incident response (IR) hooks for access/accountability failures:
- On suspicious elevation: immediate revoke of active session badges, capture of session recording, collect network traces (pcap snippet), and snapshot of related policies.
- Notify compliance and the customer success owner where relevant.
- Preserve evidence bundle with legal hold if requested.

Operational checklists (quick run):
- New dedicated deployment: run role-binding linter, confirm cluster-operator deny of data:Decrypt, validate SIEM mapping file, enable automatic evidence snapshots (first snapshot post-provision).
- Hosted tenant escalation request: verify two-person approval tokens exist, confirm masking policy in place, record approval IDs in audit event.
- Private air-gapped: validate evidence signing key exchange, confirm offline artifact transfer process, verify contractually-agreed retention.

Validation and auditing tools (quick references):
- Role-binding linter: github.com/redwood-inference/tools/role-linter (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- Audit schema validator: jsonschema rules in infra repo (refs in linked artifacts).
- Evidence verifier: utility that checks signature + digest + manifest.

Open questions / follow-ups (to resolve in next sprint):
- Define exact retention SLAs per customer tier (hosted free vs enterprise).
- Lockdown matrix for cross-tenant admin actions (PlatformAdmin exceptions).
- Standardize SIEM field names with GTM and customers to reduce onboarding friction.

Appendix A: Example audit event (ndjson single line) - example:
{"event_id":"b2f6a6b7-0bb8-4c65-9fa4-1a2b3c4d5e6f","timestamp":"2026-02-20T15:12:02Z","service":"control-plane","environment":"dedicated","region":"us-west-2","actor_id":"user:diego.martinez","actor_roles":["ModelDeployEngineer"],"action":"model.rollout","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"model:abc123","result":"success","request_id":"trace-1234abcd","request_context":"{"ip":"34.12.5.6","user_agent":"infra-cli/1.2.0"}","evidence_ref":"s3://redwood-evidence/dedicated/customer-xyz/snap-2026-02-20-1512.tar.gz"}

Appendix B: Quick templates and links (one-line)
- JIT flow automation: Jira ZENDESK playbook: JIRA-SEC-4821
- Role linter: PR #821 in infra tools (linked).
- SIEM onboarding checklist: confluence page link in linked_artifacts.
